thread_text:
morgan: Heads up — southcentral canaries (sc-2 pool) started failing provisioning after last-night driver 550 rollout. 7/100 nodes stuck, 3/3 canaries failed. :eyes:

kai: Seeing same. Provisioning hangs on 'running dkms build' step, CPU pinned, nv-host modules never appear. Logs show repeated `/usr/src` symlink updates then gcc OOMs on build hosts.

morgan: Quick numbers: 7 failed, 12 degraded (slow boot), rest healthy. Affected images: ubuntu-22.04 + custom cuda-toolkit-12.1. Canaries hit at 03:12 UTC, propagation started at 03:40.

elena: Journal snippet from a failing node:```
Apr 12 03:13:21 ip-10-0-12-34 systemd[1]: Starting DKMS kernel module build...
Apr 12 03:13:22 kernel: modprobe: timeout while loading nvidia
Apr 12 03:13:24 dkms: running build for nvidia-550.30...
Apr 12 03:14:01 dkms: error: failed to create symlink /usr/src/nvidia-550 -> /usr/src/nvidia-550-headers-5.15.0-71-generic
Apr 12 03:14:01 dkms: error: file exists but not a symlink
```

raj: `dkms status` shows multiple concurrent builds for same module on different kernels; some installs left partial `build/` dirs. Also systemd-udev queues up and times out waiting for module nodes -> long boot.

kai: I tried SSH to one stuck node and `pkill -f dkms && dkms autoinstall` then reboot. That node came up cleanly. But doing that across fleet is manual and slow.

morgan: Can we pause the rollout? If this is a DKMS concurrency/race we're going to keep hitting more nodes.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused by pipeline at 04:02 UTC — reason: 3 failing canaries detected.

prasanna: This looks like a classic parallel-dkms race when multiple kernel-header packages are installed in the same provisioning step. Our provisioner runs `apt install -y 'nvidia-driver-550*'` which triggers several dkms builds concurrently. We should either serialize `dkms autoinstall` or set `DKMS_NUM_JOBS=1` in `/etc/default/dkms` during provisioning. Also consider adding a simple flock around `/var/lib/dkms/.dkms-lock`.

elena: Quick mitigation that should be low-risk: patch cloud-init for sc-2 AMI to export `DKMS_NUM_JOBS=1` before driver package install. Can push as a hotfix to the image/build pipeline.

raj: Any chance kernel-header mismatches are amplifying this? A few nodes reported `headers for 5.15.0-71 not found` before the symlink error. If headers are missing dkms will attempt to build against whatever's there and may leave garbage.

kai: Yep saw that too — our prebaked AMI was missing the latest header meta-package. That plus parallel dkms is the perfect storm.

morgan: Plan: 1) Pause rollout (done). 2) Push cloud-init hotfix to set `DKMS_NUM_JOBS=1` + ensure header meta-package present. 3) Re-run canaries after 2h. 4) If still flaky, rollback the driver to 535 for sc pools. I'm patching infra-ops runbook now.

prasanna: I'll open a quick PR with the flock wrapper and a short test to simulate concurrent installs. If we want faster mitigation, updating the AMI with `DKMS_NUM_JOBS=1` is easiest.

morgan: Going to escalate to oncall and notify support SRE to standby for MTR and node remediation. Will update thread with links to PR and rollback playbook. :thumbsup:

kai: Also tagging cost/ops — provisioning retries increase instance hours but it's small compared to downtime. I'll file a quick FYI to finance bucket if we keep manual remediations.

sre-bot: Created incident INC-2026-042: "dkms concurrency causing driver 550 provisioning failures — sc-2". Pager duty notified.

morgan: Thanks everyone. I expect a hotfix + canary re-run in ~2 hours, will post results.
